title: Python Keyword and Positional Arguments
learningObjectives: Explain the behavior of python keyword and positional arguments.
Write and call functions using appropriate parameter forms.
Predict argument binding, scope and return behavior.
Choose suitable function constructs for a practical task.
Apply readable function design and avoid common pitfalls.

understand.concept: Python function calls can pass arguments positionally or by keyword. Positional arguments bind according to parameter order. Keyword arguments identify a parameter by name, making calls more explicit. Positional arguments must appear before keyword arguments in a call. A parameter should not receive multiple values in one call.
understand.whyItMatters: Keyword arguments improve clarity when a function has several parameters, while positional arguments keep simple calls concise.
understand.analogy: Positional arguments are like filling form fields in order; keyword arguments label each field explicitly.
understand.analogyLimit: Function signatures may also include positional-only and keyword-only markers; this lesson covers standard parameters.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Positional calls

Arguments bind to parameters from left to right.

## 2. Keyword calls

Use `parameter=value` in a call to identify the target parameter by name.

## 3. Mix carefully

Positional arguments can precede keyword arguments. Do not place a positional argument after a keyword argument.

## 4. Avoid duplicate values

Do not provide the same parameter once positionally and again by keyword.
